rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel struck them with a terrifying cry that split their hearts and killed them.
rows.anchor: جبريل صاح عليهم صيحة هائلة تصدعت منها قلوبهم فماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This episode identifies the people as Salih's people.
rows.anchor: واستدل به على أن القوم قوم صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry came inevitably, by God's justice, or according to the true promise.
rows.anchor: بالوجه الثابت الذي لا دافع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their destruction is likened to the debris carried by a flood.
rows.anchor: شبههم في دمارهم بغثاء السيل وهو حميله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs say a valley swept someone away to mean that the person perished.
rows.anchor: كقول العرب: سال به الوادي، لمن هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may state their doom or pray for it.
rows.anchor: يحتمل الإخبار والدعاء، وبعدا مصدر بعد إذا هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan is a verbal noun from baʿuda, governed by an unexpressed verb not ordinarily stated.
rows.anchor: وهو من المصادر التي تنصب بأفعال لا يستعمل إظهارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām specifies who is prayed against; the explicit description replaces their pronoun to give the reason.
rows.anchor: واللام لبيان من دعي عليه بالبعد، ووضع الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They dismiss his message as possession, though they know he surpasses them in reason and discernment.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يعلمون أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أرجحهم عقلا وأدقهم نظرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most dislike the truth because it conflicts with their desires, so they reject it.
rows.anchor: لأنه يخالف شهواتهم وأهواءهم فلذلك أنكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reject belief from disdain at their people's reproach or from little intelligence and reflection, rather than hatred of truth.
rows.anchor: لقلة فطنته وعدم فكرته لا كراهة للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If reality accommodated their desire for multiple gods, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
rows.anchor: بأن كان في الواقع آلهة شتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument repeats that multiple gods would corrupt the cosmos.
rows.anchor: لو كان فيهما ءالهة إلا الله لفسدتا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading says that if truth followed their desires and became falsehood, the world's order would vanish and nothing remain.
rows.anchor: لو اتبع الحق أهواءهم وانقلب باطلا لذهب ما قام به العالم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says that if Muhammad's truth became their desired idolatry, God would bring the Resurrection and destroy the world in anger.
rows.anchor: أو لو اتبع الحق الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أهواءهم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: On the Muʿtazilite principle, granting their desire for shirk and sins would make God cease to be God and unable to sustain creation.
rows.anchor: وهو على أصل المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reminder is the Book, as admonition or renown.
rows.anchor: بالكتاب الذي هو ذكرهم أي وعظهم أو صيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the reminder they had wished for in an earlier claim.
rows.anchor: الذكر الذي تمنوه بقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has bi-dhikrāhum.
rows.anchor: لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين } وقرىء «بذكراهم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from the reminder instead of attending to it.
rows.anchor: { فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون } لا يلتفتون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alternative question corresponds to the earlier question whether he was possessed.
rows.anchor: قسيم قوله { أم به جنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj means payment for delivering the message.
rows.anchor: أجرا على أداء الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's kharāj is either sustenance in this life or reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: رزقه في الدنيا أو ثوابه في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's provision is better for its breadth and permanence, leaving the Messenger no need to take their payment.
rows.anchor: لسعته ودوامه ففيه مندوحة لك عن عطائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj is what one gives another; kharāj usually means land tax, suggesting abundant, continuing payment.
rows.anchor: والخرج بإزاء الدخل يقال لكل ما تخرجه إلى غيرك

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads kharjan fa-kharjun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر «خرجا فخرج»

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read khirājan fa-kharāj for matching sound-patterns.
rows.anchor: وحمزة والكسائي «خراجا فخراج» للمزاوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause confirms the superiority of God's provision.
rows.anchor: تقرير لخيرية خراجه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound minds attest that the path is straight, with no deviation to justify accusing the Messenger.
rows.anchor: تشهد العقول السليمة على استقامته لا عوج فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses eliminate grounds for denial and accusation, leaving hatred of truth or lack of discernment.
rows.anchor: حصر أقسام ما يؤدي إلى الإنكار والاتهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs point to laws and good manners so people may take heed and learn proper conduct.
rows.anchor: الدالة على الشرائع ومحاسن الآداب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every circumstance and is wise in governance; indecency cannot be attributed to His Prophet or approved by Him.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز الكشخنة على نبيه ولا يقرره عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who love the spread of indecency are those who desire it to become widespread.
rows.anchor: { إن الذين يحبون } يريدون. { أن تشيع } أن تنتشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who desire indecency to spread among believers face painful punishment in this world and the next, including legal penalties and Hellfire.
rows.anchor: { الفحشة في الذين ءامنوا لهم عذاب أليم فى الدنيا والأخرة } بالحد والسعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows concealed thoughts while people do not; people punish outward evidence, and God punishes the inward wish to spread scandal.
rows.anchor: { والله يعلم } ما في الضمائر. { وأنتم لا تعلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the mention of God's favor and mercy recalls His delay of punishment, underscoring the offense's gravity.
rows.anchor: تكرير للمنة بترك المعاجلة بالعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that God is compassionate and merciful is coordinated with His favor; the conditional answer is omitted because already stated.
rows.anchor: على حصول فضله ورحمته عليهم وحذف الجواب وهو مستغنى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here following Satan's steps means spreading indecency.
rows.anchor: بإشاعة الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read with an open ṭāʾ; Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr, and Ḥamza read it with sukūn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح الطاء وقرأ نافع والبزي وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following clause explains why following Satan is prohibited.
rows.anchor: بيان لعلة النهي عن اتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāḥishah is extreme ugliness.
rows.anchor: و «الفحشاء» ما أفرط قبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar is what religious law rejects.
rows.anchor: و «المنكر» ما أنكره الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor includes enabling repentance that erases sins and prescribing penalties that expiate them.
rows.anchor: بتوفيق التوبة الماحية للذنوب وشرع الحدود

words: مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakā means purification from the stain of sin, forever.
rows.anchor: ما طهر من دنسها. { منكم من أحد أبدا } آخر الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purifies whom He wills by guiding that person to repentance and accepting it.
rows.anchor: بحمله على التوبة وقبولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what they say and knows their intentions.
rows.anchor: { والله سميع } لمقالهم. { عليم } بنياتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾtal can mean swearing, from al-aliyya, or falling short, from al-alw; the variant yataʾalla supports the first.
rows.anchor: { ولا يأتل } ولا يحلف افتعال من الألية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse came down concerning Abū Bakr, who swore he would no longer support his cousin Misṭaḥ, a poor Emigrant.
rows.anchor: وأنه نزل في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Abū Bakr religiously meritorious and wealthy indicates his virtue and honor.
rows.anchor: { أولوا الفضل منكم } في الدين. { والسعة } في المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An yuʾtū can be parsed with an omitted lā or with fī; a tāʾ reading uses grammatical shift in address.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتاء على الالتفات. { أولي القربى والمسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near relatives, poor, and Emigrants may describe one person with all three qualities or stand for several classes.
rows.anchor: صفات لموصوف واحد، أي ناسا جامعين لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should forgive transgressions and overlook them; hope for God's forgiveness should move them to forgive and imitate His character.
rows.anchor: { وليعفوا } عما فرط منهم. { وليصفحوا } بالإغماض عنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله ﷺ
rows.claim: After the Prophet recited the verse to Abū Bakr, he said he loved God's forgiveness and resumed support for Misṭaḥ.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قرأها على أبي بكر رضي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī buyūt may attach to the preceding parable as a niche in some houses, or to the lamp being kindled in houses.
rows.anchor: متعلق بما قبله أي كمشكاة في بعض بيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching it to kindling restricts the example to a fine setting, since mosque lamps are larger; it may instead depict believers' prayers or bodies as mosques.
rows.anchor: تقييد للممثل به بما يكون تحبيرا ومبالغة فيه فإن قناديل المساجد تكون أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural houses do not conflict with one niche, which denotes a type without specifying number.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي جمع البيوت وحدة المشكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it attaches to yusabbiḥ or an implied command to pray in houses; it cannot attach to yudhkar because the latter is governed by an.
rows.anchor: أو بما بعده وهو يسبح، وفيها تكرير مؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The houses are mosques, whose qualities suit the description; some say the three mosques, with indefiniteness for glorification.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها المساجد لأن الصفة تلائمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God permitted the houses to be raised in construction or elevated through honor.
rows.anchor: بالبناء أو التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's name includes mention of His acts and discussion of His rulings.
rows.anchor: عام فيما يتضمن ذكره حتى المذاكرة في أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent and here refers to prayer in mornings and evenings.
rows.anchor: ينزهونه أي يصلون له فيها بالغدوات والعشيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghudu is a verbal noun used for morning time, paired with āṣāl, the plural of aṣīl.
rows.anchor: والغدو مصدر أطلق للوقت ولذلك حسن اقترانه بالآصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has al-īṣāl, meaning entry into the evening.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع أصيل، وقرىء «والإيصال» وهو الدخول في الأصيل

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read yusabbiḥ with fatḥa, assigning it to a time expression and raising rijāl by implication.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر «يسبح» بالفتح على إسناده إلى أحد الظروف الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read tusabbiḥ with kasra for feminine plural agreement, or with fatḥa assigned to morning times.
rows.anchor: وقرىء تسبح بالتاء مكسورا لتأنيث الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their profitable business does not distract them from remembrance, prayer, or almsgiving.
rows.anchor: لا تشغلهم معاملة رابحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sale may generalize after trade, or single out the more important half of commerce, where profit is realized, unlike hoped-for gain in buying.
rows.anchor: ولا بيع عن ذكر الله } مبالغة بالتعميم بعد التخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some understand trade as buying, its origin; others as importing, the common form, as in usage for bringing goods.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالتجارة الشراء فإنه أصلها ومبدؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of commerce hints that these worshippers are merchants.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء بأنهم تجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In iqām, the genitive construction replaces the tāʾ compensating for a weak root letter lost through phonetic change; a cited line illustrates the form.
rows.anchor: الإضافة من التاء المعوضة عن العين الساقطة بالإعلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh is what must be paid from property to its rightful recipients.
rows.anchor: ما يجب إخراجه من المال للمستحقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fear the coming day even while engaged in remembrance and obedience.
rows.anchor: مع ما هم عليه من الذكر والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts and eyes may shake from terror, or their capacities may turn to perceive what they had not perceived.
rows.anchor: تضطرب وتتغير من الهول، أو تتقلب أحوالها فتفقه القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hearts turn between hope of rescue and fear of ruin, while eyes search how they will be taken and receive their records.
rows.anchor: مع توقع النجاة وخوف الهلاك والأبصار من أي ناحية يؤخذ بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describing dominion may be an appositive to the first noun, or an expression of praise in the nominative or accusative.
rows.anchor: بدل من الأول أو مدح مرفوع أو منصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of a child refutes the Christian claim.
rows.anchor: كزعم النصارى

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of a partner refutes the dualists; God has absolute dominion without a rival or co-owner.
rows.anchor: كقول الثنوية أثبت له الملك مطلقا ونفى ما يقوم مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He originated everything with measures suited to His will, including human materials, forms, and shapes.
rows.anchor: أحدثه إحداثا مراعى فيه التقدير حسب إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prepared each creature for its intended traits and acts, fitting humans for perception, understanding, judgment, invention, and work.
rows.anchor: فقدره وهيأه لما أراد منه من الخصائص والأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, He appointed each creature's duration until its specified term.
rows.anchor: أو { فقدره } للبقاء إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If khalq means mere bringing into existence, He created each thing and measured its production so it would not be uneven.
rows.anchor: وأوجد كل شيء فقدره في إيجاده حتى لا يكون متفاوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with Muhammad, God appointed criminal enemies for every prophet, so Muhammad should be patient as earlier prophets were.
rows.anchor: كما جعلناه لك فاصبر كما صبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is evidence that God creates evil; ʿaduww may be singular or plural.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه خالق الشر، والعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices to guide the Prophet to overpower his enemies and to support him against them.
rows.anchor: وكفى بربك هاديا } إلى طريق قهرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is understood as passive anzala, as in a verb meaning reported, so it does not conflict with the demand for one descent.
rows.anchor: أي أنزل عليه كخبر بمعنى أخبر لئلا يناقض قوله: { جملة وحدة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection has no force: the Qur'an's miraculousness is unchanged whether revealed all at once or in parts.
rows.anchor: لأن الإعجاز لا يختلف بنزوله جملة أو مفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual revelation strengthened Muhammad's heart for memorization and understanding; unlike Moses, David, and Jesus, he was unlettered and might have been overwhelmed by an all-at-once revelation.
rows.anchor: فتقوى بتفريقه فؤادك على حفظه وفهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation with events gave deeper insight; each installment that opponents could not match strengthened his heart.
rows.anchor: ولأن نزوله بحسب الوقائع يوجب مزيد بصيرة وغوص في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's repeated arrival strengthened the Prophet; gradual revelation also disclosed abrogation and joined situational context to verbal evidence, aiding eloquence.
rows.anchor: ولأنه إذا نزل به جبريل حالا بعد حال يثبت به فؤاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika may refer to omitted gradual sending, or remain part of the disbelievers' speech and refer to earlier books; the lām attaches to an omitted phrase either way.
rows.anchor: وكذلك صفة مصدر محذوف والإشارة إلى إنزاله مفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recited the Qur'an to Muhammad bit by bit, deliberately and calmly, over twenty or twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: وقرأناه عليك شيئا بعد شيء على تؤدة وتمهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root image of tartīl is the spacing of the teeth.
rows.anchor: وأصل الترتيل في الأسنان وهو تفليجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night's darkness is likened to clothing because it covers people.
rows.anchor: شبه ظلامه باللباس في ستره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep is rest because it cuts off occupations, or death, as in 6:60, because it cuts life; al-masbūt means dead.
rows.anchor: راحة للأبدان بقطع المشاغل، وأصل السبت القطع أو موتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is spreading forth for livelihood, or rising from sleep analogous to resurrection.
rows.anchor: ذا نشور أي انتشار ينتشر فيه الناس للمعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep and waking foreshadow death and resurrection.
rows.anchor: النوم واليقظة أنموذج للموت والنشور

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqmān tells his son that waking after sleep is like being raised after death.
rows.anchor: يا بني كما تنام فتوقظ كذلك تموت فتنشر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads al-rīḥ in the singular to mean the generic wind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير على التوحيد إرادة للجنس

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads nushran with sukūn for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بالسكون على التخفيف

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read nushran with sukūn and fatḥa on the nūn, treating it as a verbal noun used descriptively.
rows.anchor: وحمزة والكسائي به وبفتح النون على أنه مصدر وصف به

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads bushran, a light form of bushur, plural of bushūr meaning bearer of good news.
rows.anchor: وعاصم { بشرا } تخفيف بشر جمع بشور بمعنى مبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before God's mercy means ahead of the rain.
rows.anchor: يعني قدام المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭahūr means purifying, supported by 8:11; it names what is used for purification, like wuḍūʾ and waqūd.
rows.anchor: مطهرا لقوله { ليطهركم به }

rows.speaker: رسول الله ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet said that earth is a purifier for the believer.
rows.anchor:
قال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" التراب طهور المؤمن "

rows.speaker: رسول الله ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet said a vessel licked by a dog is purified by washing it seven times, one with earth.
rows.anchor: طهور إناء أحدكم إذا ولغ الكلب فيه أن يغسل سبعا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take ṭahūr to mean exceptionally pure; the form can denote a patient, an action, or an instrument.
rows.anchor: وقيل بليغا في الطهارة وفعول وإن غلب في المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the water ṭahūr signals its blessing: pure water is more pleasant and useful than water whose purity is impaired.
rows.anchor: وتوصيف الماء به إشعارا بالنعمة فيه وتتميم للمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If outward forms require purification, inner selves have an even greater need.
rows.anchor: ظواهرهم لما كانت مما ينبغي أن يطهروها فبواطنهم بذلك أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic tongue is clear in meaning, leaving no excuse of incomprehension; the phrase attaches to the revelation.
rows.anchor: واضح المعنى لئلا يقولوا ما نصنع بما لا نفهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it attaches to the warned ones, identifying Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Ishmael, Shuʿayb, and Muhammad as warned in Arabic.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق بالمنذرين أي لتكون ممن أنذروا بلغة العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is in the earlier books is either the Qur'an's mention or its meaning.
rows.anchor: وإن ذكره أو معناه لفي الكتب المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite scholars' knowledge is a sign of the Qur'an's truth or Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: على صحة القرآن أو نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite scholars recognize the Qur'an from descriptions in their books, establishing it as evidence.
rows.anchor: أن يعرفوه بنعته المذكور في كتبهم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads takun with feminine agreement and āyatun in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر تكن بالتاء و { ءاية } بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading āyah may be the subject with lahum as predicate and an yaʿlamahu an appositive or agent; alternatively it may be a pronoun-of-affair construction.
rows.anchor: على أنها الاسم والخبر { لهم } { وأن يعلمه } بدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening may mean remember the story when Moses spoke, or attach to ʿalīm.
rows.anchor: أي اذكر قصته { إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānastu means that Moses perceived a fire.
rows.anchor: إني آنست نارا } أي اذكر قصته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He promises news about the road because he had lost the way.
rows.anchor: أي عن حال الطريق لأنه قد ضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address may be used although his only companion was his wife, since ahl can euphemistically denote a wife.
rows.anchor: وجمع الضمير إن صح أنه لم يكن معه غير امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future marker indicates distance and a promise to come even if delayed.
rows.anchor: والسين للدلالة على بعد المسافة والوعد بالإتيان وإن أبطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shihāb qabas is a flame taken from another; the annexation distinguishes it from a flame that is not a brand.
rows.anchor: شعلة نار مقبوسة، وإضافة الشهاب إليه

rows.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Kufans and Yaʿqūb pronounce the nūn in qabasun, making qabas an appositive or description meaning seized.
rows.anchor: ونونه الكوفيون ويعقوب على أن ال { قبس } بدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offers are tentative, as in Ṭā Hā; if Moses obtains neither, he expects at least one by ordinary expectation or trust that God will not combine two deprivations.
rows.anchor: والعدتان على سبيل الظن ولذلك عبر عنهما بصيغة الترجي في «طه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman is Bilqīs, daughter of Sharaḥīl ibn Mālik ibn al-Rayyān; the pronouns refer to Sabaʾ or its people.
rows.anchor: يعني بلقيس بنت شراحيل بن مالك بن الريان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She had everything a ruler needs.
rows.anchor: يحتاج إليه الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne is great relative to her or comparable thrones; reports give thirty cubits in each dimension or eighty of gold and silver adorned with gems.
rows.anchor: عظمه بالنسبة إليها أو إلى عروش أمثالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen and her people worshipped the sun instead of God, and Satan adorned that and their other vile deeds.
rows.anchor: وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan turned them from the path of truth and right guidance.
rows.anchor: عن سبيل الحق والصواب. { فهم لا يهتدون } إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allā yasjudū may mean Satan blocked them lest they prostrate or adorned their refusal; alternatively, they fail to find the way to prostration with an extra lā.
rows.anchor: فصدهم لئلا يسجدوا أو زين لهم أن لا يسجدوا

rows.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read illā with a light hamza as a call to attention, with an omitted addressee: O people, prostrate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ويعقوب { إلا } بالتخفيف على أنها للتنبيه ويا للنداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light reading permits a new divine or Solomonic command after a pause at lā yahtadūn; the other rebukes refusal, and both imply prostration is obligatory generally, not necessarily on recitation.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا صح أن يكون استئنافا من الله أو من سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings include halā with hamza changed to hāʾ and direct-address forms alā tasjudūn and halā tasjudūn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «هلا» و «هلا» بقلب الهمزة هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates the attention-getting vocative construction.
rows.anchor: وقالت ألا يا اسمع أعظك بخطة

words: ٱلَّذِى يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabʾ is something hidden within another; bringing it out means revealing it.
rows.anchor: و { الخبء } ما خفي في غيره وإخراجه إظهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings forth shining stars, falling rain, sprouting plants, creation actualized from potential, and origination from possibility and nonexistence.
rows.anchor: وهو يعم إشراق الكواكب وإنزال الأمطار وإنبات النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the Necessary Existent has power to bring things from possibility and nonexistence into existence.
rows.anchor: ما في الإمكان والعدم إلى الوجوب والوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's perfect power and knowledge entitle Him alone to worship, urging prostration and refuting worship of others.
rows.anchor: بما يوجب اختصاصه باستحقاق السجود من التفرد

rows.speaker: حفص والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī read the verbs with tāʾ, addressing listeners directly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص والكسائي »ما تخفون وما تعلنون« بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was returned to his mother so she would rejoice and not grieve over separation.
rows.anchor: فرددنه إلى أمه كى تقر عينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She would learn by witnessing that God's promise was true; alternatively, her knowledge was the primary purpose and the return secondary, implicitly recalling her earlier lapse.
rows.anchor: { ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق } علم مشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd is full development, beyond which growth does not increase; this is placed at thirty to forty when reason matures.
rows.anchor: مبلغه الذي لا يزيد عليه نشؤه وذلك من ثلاثين إلى أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says every prophet was commissioned at forty.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لم يبعث نبي إلا على رأس الأربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā may refer to Moses' stature or intellect.
rows.anchor: { واستوى } قده أو عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥukm means prophethood, while ʿilm means knowledge of religion.
rows.anchor: حكما } أي نبوة. { وعلما } بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God gave him the bearing and knowledge of scholars before prophethood, so he would not act foolishly; this better fits the narrative order.
rows.anchor: أو علم الحكماء والعلماء وسمتهم قبل استنبائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards benefactors as He rewarded Moses and his mother.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الذي فعلنا بموسى وأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people Moses escaped were Pharaoh and his followers.
rows.anchor: نجوت من القوم الظلمين } يريد فرعون وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daughter who spoke was the one who summoned Moses.
rows.anchor: قالت إحداهما } يعني التي استدعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She proposed hiring Moses to tend sheep.
rows.anchor: يعني التي استدعته. { يأبت استأجره } لرعي الغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling strength and trustworthiness the best grounds for hiring is a common maxim functioning as proof; the past tense presents Moses as tested and known.
rows.anchor: تعليل شائع يجري مجرى الدليل على أنه حقيق بالاستئجار

rows.speaker: شعيب
rows.claim: When Shuʿayb asked how she knew Moses was strong, she described him lifting a stone, lowering his head so she could convey the message, and telling her to walk behind him.
rows.anchor: روي أن شعيبا قال لها وما أعلمك بقوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ujūrani means Moses hire himself to the father or work as his employee, or give back some of what God rewards him.
rows.anchor: أي تأجر نفسك مني أو تكون لي أجيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight seasons is an adverbial duration on the first two readings, but an object on the third with sheep-tending understood.
rows.anchor: ظرف على الأولين ومفعول به على الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing ten years would be Moses' voluntary generosity, not an obligation imposed by the father.
rows.anchor: فمن عندك } فإتمامه من عندك تفضلا لا من عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a request to make a marriage contract, not the contract itself; possible explanations include separate wage and dowry, an optional extension, the sheep belonging to the bride, or differing laws.
rows.anchor: وهذا استدعاء العقد لا نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father would not burden Moses with an obligatory tenth year or strict scrutiny of schedules and completed work.
rows.anchor: بإلزام إتمام العشر أو المناقشة في مراعاة الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of hardship is splitting: what is difficult seems to split belief in one's capacity and judgment about undertaking it.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق المشقة من الشق فإن ما يصعب عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He promises good treatment, gentleness, and faithful fulfillment of the agreement.
rows.anchor: في حسن المعاملة ولين الجانب والوفاء بالمعاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gifts mentioned are worldly means.
rows.anchor: { وما أوتيتم من شيء } من أسباب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly means provide enjoyment and adornment only during this finite life.
rows.anchor: تتمتعون وتتزينون به مدة حياتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is with God refers to His reward.
rows.anchor: وهو ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward is better as complete delight and pleasure, and more enduring because everlasting.
rows.anchor: { خير } في نفسه من ذلك لأنه لذة خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question urges people to exchange the lower worldly good for what is better.
rows.anchor: فتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads with yāʾ, making the admonition more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بالياء وهو أبلغ في الموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good promise is Paradise; its recipient certainly attains it because God does not break His promise, hence the causal faʾ.
rows.anchor: مدركه لا محالة لامتناع الخلف في وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person granted worldly enjoyment receives something mixed with pain and difficulty, followed by grief when it ends.
rows.anchor: مشوب بالآلام مكدر بالمتاعب مستعقب بالتحسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly recipient will be brought for judgment or punishment; thumma marks temporal or rank delay.
rows.anchor: للحساب أو العذاب، و { ثم } للتراخي في الزمان

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, and al-Kisāʾī read thumma huwa with a quiescent hāʾ by analogy to a connected pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر في رواية والكسائي { ثم هو } بسكون الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse concludes the previous one and is joined to it with faʾ.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية كالنتيجة للتي قبلها ولذلك رتبت عليها بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was revealed as revelation confirming the divine books and fulfilling the statement that scripture recipients believe in it.
rows.anchor: وحيا مصدقا لسائر الكتب الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given scripture who believe may be ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and peers, or earlier People of the Book.
rows.anchor: هم عبد الله بن سلام وأضرابه، أو من تقدم عهد الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers from among these may mean Arabs, Meccans, or contemporaneous Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب أو أهل مكة أو ممن في عهد الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those deeply entrenched in disbelief deny the signs; their conviction keeps them from considering evidence of the Qur'an's miracle through the Messenger.
rows.anchor: مع ظهورها وقيام الحجة عليها

words: وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَٰبٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unlettered Prophet's delivery of a book gathering noble sciences despite not reading is extraordinary evidence.
rows.anchor: فإن ظهور هذا الكتاب الجامع لأنواع العلوم الشريفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the right hand makes the negation vivid and rules out figurative attribution of writing.
rows.anchor: وذكر اليمين زيادة تصوير للمنفي ونفي للتجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he had read or written, falsifiers would suspect that he learned or copied from earlier scriptures; they are so named for disbelief or doubt despite many proofs.
rows.anchor: لو كنت ممن يخط ويقرأ لقالوا لعله تعلمه أو التقطه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says People of the Book would doubt because the Prophet's description differed from their scriptures; they would be falsifiers in actuality, not hypothetically.
rows.anchor: وقيل لارتاب أهل الكتاب لوجدانهم نعتك على خلاف ما في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling this life insignificant expresses contempt; with God it weighs less than a mosquito's wing.
rows.anchor: إشارة تحقير وكيف لا وهي لا تزن عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life resembles children's play: they gather and enjoy it briefly, then part exhausted.
rows.anchor: إلا كما يلهى ويلعب به الصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is true life because death cannot reach it, or it is life itself by an intensive expression.
rows.anchor: لهي دار الحياة الحقيقية لامتناع طريان الموت عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥayawān is a verbal noun of ḥayya used for a living being; originally ḥayayan, its second yāʾ changed to wāw.
rows.anchor: { الحيوان } مصدر حي سمي به ذو الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥayawān is more emphatic than ḥayāh because faʿalān suggests life's movement and agitation.
rows.anchor: وهو أبلغ من الحياة لما في بناء فعلان من الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they knew, they would not prefer worldly life, whose life is incidental, brief, and rooted in nonlife.
rows.anchor: لم يؤثروا عليها الدنيا التي أصلها عدم الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next account develops the description: at sea they call on God alone, knowing only He can remove distress.
rows.anchor: متصل بما دل عليه شرح حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God brings them safely to land, they suddenly return to associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving relatives their due includes maintaining kinship ties.
rows.anchor: { فئات ذا القربى حقه } كصلة الرحم،

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: The Ḥanafīs cite this for obligatory maintenance of unmarriageable relatives, but al-Bayḍāwī says the verse does not establish that ruling.
rows.anchor: واحتج به الحنفية على وجوب النفقة للمحارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor and traveler receive the portions assigned to them from alms.
rows.anchor: { والمسكين وابن السبيل } ما وظف لهما من الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet or whoever has means; the faʾ links the command to what precedes.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو لمن بسط له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking His essence or direction: giving sincerely or intending closeness rather than another end.
rows.anchor: ذاته أو جهته أي يقصدون بمعروفهم إياه خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who give this way succeed by gaining abiding bliss through what God granted them.
rows.anchor: حيث حصلوا بما بسط لهم النعيم المقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribā here is an unlawful transaction increase or a gift expecting greater compensation.
rows.anchor: زيادة محرمة في المعاملة أو عطية يتوقع بها مزيد مكافأة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads ribā in the shortened form, meaning what you bring by giving an increase.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير بالقصر بمعنى ما جئتم به من إعطاء ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver seeks to increase or make the recipient's wealth grow.
rows.anchor: ليزيد ويزكو في أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That increase does not grow with God, become pure, or receive blessing.
rows.anchor: فلا يزكو عنده ولا يبارك فيه

rows.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read li-tarbū, meaning you increase or become characterized by ribā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ويعقوب «لتربوا» أي لتزيدوا أو لتصيروا

words: وَمَآ ءَاتَيتُم مِّن زَكَوٰةٍۢ تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving alms seeking God's face means seeking Him sincerely.
rows.anchor: تريدون وجه الله } تبتغون به وجهه خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḍʿifūn may mean possessors of multiplied reward or those whose reward and property charity multiplies; the form resembles words for strength or wealth.
rows.anchor: ذوو الأضعاف من الثواب ونظير المضعف المقوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading opens the ʿayn; its departure from parallel phrasing intensifies the meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح العين وتغييره عن سنن المقابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to third person exalts recipients before angels and elite creatures or generalizes the statement to anyone who does this.
rows.anchor: والالتفات فيه للتعظيم كأنه خاطب به الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā is relative, the omitted return is al-muḍʿifūna bihi; alternatively, the ellipsis is fa-muʾtūhu ulāʾika hum al-muḍʿifūn.
rows.anchor: والراجع منه محذوف إن جعلت ما موصولة تقديره المضعفون به
